beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Riley's back between takes, headphones still hooked around her neck.

beats.prompt: The past: the choice about the writing partnership, weighed and made.
The present: the space you finally claimed as yours.
The future: the trust you're building with someone else's ear.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Quiz me. If the Hierophant's about trusting a mentor, am I supposed to just do whatever the producer says now, no pushback?"

options.text: No — it's a bridge, not a leash. You still bring your own voice across it.
Yes, pushback isn't allowed once you trust someone.
This card doesn't involve pushback either way.

elaboration: It's a bridge between the everyday and the sacred, not a substitute for it — rejecting all guidance is one extreme, but handing over every call is the other.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "What if leaning on him just means I don't trust my own ear anymore?"

options.text: Leaning on something steady when things feel shaky isn't the same as losing yourself.
It is — you should trust no one but yourself.
Trusting yourself isn't part of this card.

elaboration: When reality feels shaky, lean on faith or tradition to steady it — that's borrowing steadiness, not surrendering your own ear.

beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: "One thread ties all three: the partnership you chose, the space you claimed, and now, a voice you've decided is worth trusting."

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Yeah. I think trusting him doesn't cancel out trusting myself — I just get to do both at once. Thanks for that."
